findings.summary: The prepared-without-commit recovery path cannot restore the promised exact pre-state because the journal stores post-state bytes but only preimage hashes/metadata, then requires exact pre-state after target replacement without recoverable old bytes.
findings.verbatim_body: The journal stores only post-state bytes as staged blobs; for pre-state it records hashes and metadata, not recoverable preimage content. After target replacement, recovery nevertheless requires exact pre-state when no commit marker exists. It neither rolls back targets already equal to their postimages nor identifies where their preimage bytes can be recovered. A crash after one or more replacements can therefore leave mixed pre/post targets with no defined mechanism to reconstruct the old bytes. The mismatch path is also contradictory: lines 87–90 propose restoring a target whose hash is neither preimage nor postimage, while lines 94–95 require that same condition to fail closed for manual intervention.
findings.required_repair: Either stage and durably record content-addressed preimage bytes and explicitly roll every postimage target back before clearing an uncommitted transaction, or define deterministic roll-forward from prepared state. Specify one conflict-free rule for unexpected hashes.

limitations: Reviewer did not inspect implementation code, run validators/doctor/product proofs, inspect or mutate #114, consult the live issue body, or verify implementation behavior.

The supplied R2 artifact hashes matched exactly, and its retained record correctly binds the immutable snapshot while marking original line references as historical rather than current live-line proof.
disposition: retained_as_prebind_design_review_failure; repaired through prepared design and typed card updates before any approval, bind, or implementation
